the heteroatom in the five-membered heteroring is a weaker electron acceptor than the corresponding heteroatom in benzene.

the conductivity in the heterorings is determined by the heteroatom and is lower than in the benzene ring, while the conductivity of the heteroaromatic ring in the unpaired electron level depends on both the heteroatom in the ring and the substituent in the ring.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electron affininity of heterorings is determined mainly by the electronegativity of the heteroatomic nucleus, while the electron density of the unpaired spin in the level of its localization is determined by both the electronegativities of the heteronuclear atom and by the conductivity of the substituents through the heteroring.

the heteroatoms of furan, benzofuran, thiophene and benzothiophene rings in the level of unpaired electron are more electron deficient than in the ground state.
